div.l: That fro þe tyme of kyng william were fall
Ther to he koude endite and make a thing
There koude no man pynche at his writyng
And eủer statut koude he plein by rote
He rode but homely in a medle Cote
Girt wᵗith a seint of silke wᵗith barres smale
Of array telle I no lenger tale
A Fraunkelyn was in þis cumpaigne
White was his berde as ys the dayse
Of his complexcou he was sangwyn
Wele loued he by þe morow a sop in wyn
To lyf in delit was eủer his wonne
For he was Epiours owen sonne
That helde opyneou þat plein delite
Was verray felicitee ꝑperfite
An housholder and þat a grete was he
The grettest of all his cuntre
His brede his ale was alwey after one
A better wyned man was nowher none
Wᵗith out bake mete was neủer his hous
Of fissh and flessh and þᵗat so plenteuous
It sewed in his hous of mete and drynk
Of all deintes þat ony man koude thynk
After þe sondry sesons of þe yere
So chaunged he his mete and his sopere
Full many a fat partryk hade he in mue
And many a breme and many a luce in stue
Wo was his coke but yf his sauce were
Poynaunt and sharp and redy all his gere
His table . dormant in his hall all wey
Stode redy coủerde all þe longe day
At þe sessiones þere was he lord and sire
Full often tyme he was knight of þᵉ shire
And an Anlaas and a Gipcere of silk
Hing at his gurdell as white as morow milk
A sheref hade he be of a Countour
Was nowher swich a worthy vauasour
An habdassher and a Carpenter
A webber a dyer and a tapicer
And þei were clothed al in oo liủeree
